When these leaders survived assassinatio.Napoleon (Christmas Eve bomb): A cart of gunpowder exploded on Rue Saint-Nicaise just after he passed, killing several bystanders.
When these leaders survived assassinatio.Andrew Jackson: Richard Lawrence's two pistols both misfired, and Jackson reportedly then beat him with his cane.
When these leaders survived assassinatio.Queen Victoria: Edward Oxford fired two pistols at her carriage, and she survived at least seven attempts on her life.
When these leaders survived assassinatio.Theodore Roosevelt: Shot in Milwaukee while campaigning, he gave his speech anyway. A folded speech and his glasses case slowed the bullet.
When these leaders survived assassinatio.Vladimir Lenin: Fanny Kaplan shot him, leaving bullets in his body, and the attack helped spark the Red Terror.
When these leaders survived assassinatio.Hitler (July plot): Stauffenberg's bomb was shifted behind a table leg that shielded Hitler from the blast.
When these leaders survived assassinatio.Harry Truman: Puerto Rican nationalists attacked Blair House while Truman was upstairs; a guard and one attacker died.
When these leaders survived assassinatio.Charles de Gaulle: An ambush at Petit-Clamart riddled his car with bullets and inspired the novel The Day of the Jackal.
When these leaders survived assassinatio.Gerald Ford: Two attempts came within 17 days in September 1975, one by Lynette 'Squeaky' Fromme.
When these leaders survived assassinatio.Ronald Reagan: John Hinckley shot him, and he reportedly told his wife in hospital, 'Honey, I forgot to duck.'

Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Gold: It heats up easily with little energy, so a gold nugget warms fast in sunlight.
Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Silver: The best conductor of heat and electricity among metals.
Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Iron: Cast-iron pans heat slowly yet hold heat well because they are heavy and thick.
Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Aluminium: Light and common in cookware, it takes about twice as much energy per gram as iron to warm.
Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Air: Per gram it needs about as much as aluminium, but air is so light that a room's air holds little heat.
Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Ice: It holds about half of liquid water's heat capacity per gram.
Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Ethanol: It heats faster than water, so spirits warm quicker than water on a stove.
Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Liquid water: It is the highest of any common liquid, which is why oceans moderate coastal climates.
Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Helium gas: Even though it is an inert gas, light helium atoms mean lots of them per gram, so lots of energy.
Specific heat: energy to warm 1 gram by.Hydrogen gas: It is the highest of any gas per gram, because molecules so light mean enormous numbers of them per gram.

When these board games were first publis.Monopoly: Its roots lie in Lizzie Magie's 1904 Landlord's Game, designed to show the evils of land monopolies.
When these board games were first publis.Clue (Cluedo): British musician Anthony Pratt invented it during wartime air raids; it is sold as Cluedo in the UK.
When these board games were first publis.Risk: French filmmaker Albert Lamorisse created it as La Conquete du Monde, and he also made The Red Balloon.
When these board games were first publis.Twister: Its 1966 release was attacked by a rival, but Johnny Carson playing it with Eva Gabor on TV made it a hit.
When these board games were first publis.Connect Four: Milton Bradley made it, and the game is solved: the first player can always win with perfect play.
When these board games were first publis.Trivial Pursuit: Two Canadian friends invented it in Montreal in 1979, reportedly after their Scrabble set was missing pieces.
When these board games were first publis.Pictionary: Rob Angel invented it in Seattle, drawing on ideas from his waiter job.
When these board games were first publis.Catan: German designer Klaus Teuber's Settlers of Catan sparked the modern board game boom.
When these board games were first publis.Ticket to Ride: Alan Moon designed it, and it won the 2004 Spiel des Jahres.
When these board games were first publis.Codenames: With one-word clues, teammates must be steered to their agents without hitting the assassin card.

When the people these foods are named af.Bellini's painter: The Venetian painter inspired a drink at Harry's Bar, whose pink color reminded the owner of a toga in one of his paintings.
When the people these foods are named af.Carpaccio's painter: The Venetian painter's red hues inspired the raw beef dish at Harry's Bar, created for a countess who could not eat cooked meat.
When the people these foods are named af.The Earl of Sandwich: The 4th Earl is said to have demanded meat between bread so he could keep gambling without leaving the table.
When the people these foods are named af.Earl Grey: The tea, flavored with bergamot, honors a British prime minister who served in the 1830s.
When the people these foods are named af.Graham cracker's Sylvester: The health reformer wanted his plain cracker to cool desires; the vegetarian preacher was a bit of a zealot.
When the people these foods are named af.Granny Smith: An Australian orchardist, Maria Ann Smith, found the seedling in 1868 in Sydney, and her name stuck.
When the people these foods are named af.Salisbury steak's doctor: The Civil War doctor recommended minced beef patties as a healthy diet for digestive problems.
When the people these foods are named af.Pizza Margherita's queen: Legend says a pizza in 1889 honoring the queen used red, white and green toppings that matched Italy's flag.
When the people these foods are named af.Peach Melba's soprano: Chef Escoffier made the dessert for the Australian soprano, serving peaches over vanilla ice cream.
When the people these foods are named af.Pavlova's ballerina: The Russian ballerina inspired a meringue dessert, though Australia and New Zealand dispute its invention.

Melting points of household stuff.Mercury (old thermometer): Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature, and its low freezing point made it handy in thermometers, though it is toxic.
Melting points of household stuff.Vodka (freezes): Standard 40 percent vodka freezes far below a home freezer's temperature, which is why a bottle stays pourable and chilled.
Melting points of household stuff.Ice: Water is unusual because ice floats, being less dense than liquid water, so lakes freeze from the top down.
Melting points of household stuff.Coconut oil: It is solid in a cool kitchen and liquid in a warm one, thanks to saturated fats such as lauric acid.
Melting points of household stuff.Chocolate: Cocoa butter melts just below body temperature, which is why chocolate melts in your mouth but stays firm in your hand.
Melting points of household stuff.Candle wax: The flame burns vaporised wax rather than the wick itself, and only the melted pool near the flame feeds it.
Melting points of household stuff.Tin-lead solder: Traditional tin-lead solder melts low enough for delicate electronics work, though lead-free versions have largely replaced it for health reasons.
Melting points of household stuff.Lead: Its low melting point let Romans cast lead into pipes, and the Latin word for it, plumbum, gives us the word plumber.
Melting points of household stuff.Aluminium foil: Aluminium melts at about 660 degrees, yet foil is safe in a hot oven because home ovens rarely top 300 degrees.
Melting points of household stuff.Copper wire: Copper is among the best electrical conductors and was one of the first metals people learned to smelt.

When these concrete Brutalist icons were.Unité d'Habitation, Marseille: Le Corbusier's Marseille block gave the term 'béton brut', raw concrete, to Brutalism. It holds 337 flats, a rooftop nursery and an internal shopping street.
When these concrete Brutalist icons were.Park Hill, Sheffield: Sheffield's huge 'street in the sky' estate is Europe's largest listed building, with wide deck walkways that were designed to let milk floats pass.
When these concrete Brutalist icons were.Salk Institute: Louis Kahn's research institute at La Jolla frames a long water channel pointing to the Pacific, and its courtyard was reportedly advised by Luis Barragán.
When these concrete Brutalist icons were.Breuer's Whitney Museum: Marcel Breuer's Manhattan museum has a stepped, inverted-ziggurat form and a granite facade with irregular trapezoid windows, and it was later reused by other museums.
When these concrete Brutalist icons were.Boston City Hall: Its brick-and-concrete plaza design has long polarized Bostonians, and some call it an eyesore while others call it a masterpiece of civic design.
When these concrete Brutalist icons were.Preston Bus Station: The 1960s depot's curved concrete stands and car-park deck were saved from demolition in 2013 after the building won listed status.
When these concrete Brutalist icons were.Geisel Library, San Diego: William Pereira's library at UC San Diego looks like a spaceship on stilts, and is named for Theodor Geisel, better known as Dr. Seuss.
When these concrete Brutalist icons were.Trellick Tower, London: Ernő Goldfinger's 31-storey tower in west London was a landmark of Brutalist council housing, and Goldfinger the Bond villain was named after him.
When these concrete Brutalist icons were.National Theatre, London: Denys Lasdun's riverside theatre complex has three auditoriums stacked behind concrete terraces, and is named for its location on the South Bank.
When these concrete Brutalist icons were.Barbican Centre: This arts complex in the City of London is a maze of high-level walkways, with a conservatory greenhouse filled with tropical plants on its top floor.

Cards, chips and discs by longest side.Nano-SIM card: Introduced with the iPhone 5 in 2012, it is the smallest SIM type, trimmed so much that its plastic border is almost gone.
Cards, chips and discs by longest side.microSD card: Smaller than a fingernail, these cards now hold a terabyte or more, as much as many laptops stored not long ago.
Cards, chips and discs by longest side.Mini-SIM card: The first SIM cards were the size of a credit card, and the mini size was simply cut down from them, so older adapters still work.
Cards, chips and discs by longest side.SD card: SD stands for Secure Digital, and many of these cards have a tiny lock switch on the side that protects the data from being overwritten.
Cards, chips and discs by longest side.Mini CD: These held only about 20 minutes of audio, enough for a CD single, back when physical singles were a big part of pop music.
Cards, chips and discs by longest side.Credit card: Its size follows ISO standard ID-1, shared by driver's licenses and many ID cards, so wallets are built around it worldwide.
Cards, chips and discs by longest side.Audio cassette: Philips introduced the compact cassette in 1963, at first meant for office dictation, before it became the format of the mixtape.
Cards, chips and discs by longest side.Compact disc: The first CD released commercially was Billy Joel's 52nd Street, in Japan in 1982, a year before discs reached other markets.
Cards, chips and discs by longest side.Vinyl single: The 7-inch single spins at 45 rpm and was RCA's answer to the LP, designed to hold one song per side with better sound.
Cards, chips and discs by longest side.Vinyl LP: Columbia introduced the 12-inch, 33⅓ rpm record in 1948, and it could hold about 20 minutes per side, which was a huge leap.

The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Matsya the fish: The fish warned Manu of a great flood and saved the Vedas, a story with parallels to Noah.
The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Kurma the tortoise: The tortoise carried Mount Mandara on its back as the gods and demons churned the ocean of milk.
The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Varaha the boar: The boar rescued Earth from the cosmic ocean, lifting it on its tusks.
The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Narasimha the man-lion: This half man, half lion burst from a pillar at twilight to kill a demon who could not be killed by man or beast, by day or night.
The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Vamana the dwarf: This dwarf asked King Bali for three paces of land, then grew to cover the universe in two steps.
The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Parashurama: His name means Rama with the axe, and he is a sage-warrior.
The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Rama: Hero of the Ramayana, whose return to Ayodhya is celebrated at Diwali.
The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Krishna: He delivered the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield.
The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Buddha or Balarama: Traditions differ on this one: some name Balarama, Krishna's brother, others Buddha.
The ten avatars of Vishnu, in order.Kalki: He has not appeared yet; he is expected on a white horse to end the age of Kali Yuga.

From the atom to the ant.Proton: Made of three quarks, the proton is tiny; a femtometre is a quadrillionth of a metre, and a proton's width is about 1.7 of them.
From the atom to the ant.Uranium nucleus: It holds 92 protons and, in uranium-238, about 146 neutrons, making it one of the largest nuclei that occurs in nature.
From the atom to the ant.Hydrogen atom: Mostly empty space, its nucleus is about 100,000 times smaller than the atom.
From the atom to the ant.DNA double helix (width): Uncoiled, the DNA in one human cell would stretch about two metres, packed into a nucleus a fraction of a hair's width.
From the atom to the ant.Coronavirus particle: The name comes from the crown-like spikes seen in electron microscopes; corona is Latin for crown.
From the atom to the ant.E. coli bacterium: This gut resident is a lab workhorse, and it can divide every 20 minutes in ideal conditions.
From the atom to the ant.Red blood cell: It lacks a nucleus, and the body makes about two million of them every second.
From the atom to the ant.Human hair (width): A hair grows about a centimetre a month, and its width varies from person to person.
From the atom to the ant.Dust mite: A dust mite is a spider relative that eats shed skin, and it's barely visible to the naked eye.
From the atom to the ant.Ant: There are an estimated 20 quadrillion ants alive, and together they weigh about as much as people.

How long these took to build.Empire State Building: At its peak the Empire State Building rose about 4.5 floors a week, and it opened in 1931.
How long these took to build.Eiffel Tower: It was meant to be dismantled after 20 years, but was kept because it was useful as a radio antenna.
How long these took to build.Golden Gate Bridge: Its colour is called International Orange, and when it opened in 1937 it was the longest suspension bridge in the world.
How long these took to build.Channel Tunnel: British and French crews met under the seabed in 1990, and services began in 1994.
How long these took to build.Panama Canal (US effort): A French attempt failed amid disease, and the US finished the canal in 1914.
How long these took to build.Brooklyn Bridge: Washington Roebling directed it from a sickbed by looking through a window, and his wife Emily helped.
How long these took to build.Taj Mahal complex: Built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal, the main tomb was finished well before the surrounding complex.
How long these took to build.St. Peter's Basilica: Funds were partly raised by selling indulgences, which helped spark Martin Luther's protest.
How long these took to build.Notre-Dame de Paris: Construction began in 1163; a 2019 fire destroyed the spire, and it reopened in December 2024.
How long these took to build.Cologne Cathedral: Begun in 1248 and finished in 1880, it briefly became the world's tallest building until the Washington Monument.

When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Charles Martel, the Hammer: Frankish ruler whose army stopped an invasion near Tours in 732. His grandson Charlemagne built an empire on the power he gathered.
When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Louis the Pious: Charlemagne's only surviving son. After his death his own sons fought over the realm, splitting the Frankish empire.
When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Charles the Bald: Grandson of Charlemagne who took the western Frankish lands at the 843 Treaty of Verdun, the seed of the later kingdom of France.
When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Charles the Fat: He briefly reunited Charlemagne's empire, then was deposed after he bought off Vikings besieging Paris instead of fighting them.
When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Eric Bloodaxe: Last Viking king of Jorvik (York), said to have killed his own brothers. He was driven out and killed in the mid-950s.
When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Harald Bluetooth: Danish king who converted his people to Christianity. The Bluetooth wireless standard is named for him because he united warring factions.
When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Æthelred the Unready: His nickname is a pun: Old English for "ill-advised". He paid the Vikings huge tribute, and ordered the 1002 massacre of Danes in England.
When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Frederick Barbarossa: The Holy Roman Emperor nicknamed Redbeard drowned crossing a river on the Third Crusade. Legend says he sleeps under a mountain, waiting to return.
When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Richard the Lionheart: He spent only a few months of his ten-year reign in England, and was captured and held for ransom on his way home from the Crusade.
When these colorfully nicknamed rulers c.Vlad the Impaler: The Wallachian prince's cruelty and his father's title "Dracul" (dragon) inspired the name Dracula, though Bram Stoker's count is invented.

Striped animals by weight.Zebrafish: Scientists love them because their embryos are transparent, and they can regrow heart tissue.
Striped animals by weight.Zebra finch: Males learn their songs from their fathers, which makes them a favorite model for studying learning.
Striped animals by weight.Eastern chipmunk: They stash seeds in their cheek pouches and carry them to underground storage rooms.
Striped animals by weight.Numbat: This Australian marsupial eats only termites, thousands in a day, and is the emblem of Western Australia.
Striped animals by weight.Banded mongoose: They live in groups that give birth together, and they crack open eggs by smashing them against rocks.
Striped animals by weight.Striped skunk: It can spray its smelly liquid with accuracy up to around three meters.
Striped animals by weight.Thylacine: The Tasmanian tiger's last known individual died in captivity in Hobart in 1936.
Striped animals by weight.Striped hyena: It is a shy scavenger, and smaller than the spotted hyena.
Striped animals by weight.Tiger: Its stripes go skin-deep; a shaved tiger would still show the pattern.
Striped animals by weight.Plains zebra: No two have the same stripe pattern, and the stripes may help deter biting flies.

Debut year of these game franchises.Metroid: The reveal that the armored hero is a woman, Samus Aran, was a shock in the 1986 original.
Debut year of these game franchises.Final Fantasy: Named because creator Hironobu Sakaguchi thought it might be his last game, it went on for decades.
Debut year of these game franchises.Mortal Kombat: Famous for its 'Finish Him!' and fatalities, it helped prompt the creation of video game age ratings.
Debut year of these game franchises.Resident Evil: Capcom's mansion horror, with fixed cameras and door-opening loading screens, helped define survival horror.
Debut year of these game franchises.Grand Theft Auto: It began under the working title Race'n'Chase, before becoming a crime sandbox.
Debut year of these game franchises.The Sims: Will Wright's life simulator became one of the best-selling PC game franchises ever.
Debut year of these game franchises.Call of Duty: It was created by developers who had left Medal of Honor, and set the tone for modern shooters.
Debut year of these game franchises.Assassin's Creed: It began as an idea for a Prince of Persia spin-off before becoming its own series.
Debut year of these game franchises.Angry Birds: Finnish studio Rovio made it after dozens of earlier games had flopped.
Debut year of these game franchises.Candy Crush Saga: King's match-three puzzler spread on Facebook and then conquered phones.

Animal facts counted in days.An adult mayfly's life: Many adult mayflies live only hours since they don't eat; their order name, Ephemeroptera, means 'short-lived wings'.
Animal facts counted in days.A hamster's pregnancy: Gestation of a golden hamster is among the shortest of any placental mammal, and pups are born blind and hairless.
Animal facts counted in days.Chicken egg to hatching: A chick breaks out using a temporary egg tooth on its beak, and may start peeping inside the shell before hatching.
Animal facts counted in days.A summer worker bee's life: Summer workers literally work themselves to death, while winter bees can survive several months.
Animal facts counted in days.A dog's pregnancy: Pups are born with eyes shut for about their first ten days, and a dog's litter can hold a dozen or more.
Animal facts counted in days.Emperor penguin dad's fast: Each father balances a single egg on his feet through the Antarctic winter without eating while the mother feeds at sea.
Animal facts counted in days.A human pregnancy: The standard 40 weeks is counted from the last period, so actual fetal development is closer to 38 weeks.
Animal facts counted in days.An elephant's pregnancy: The longest of any land animal, about 22 months, and the calf can stand within hours of birth.
Animal facts counted in days.Periodical cicada underground: Nymphs of Magicicada spend 13 or 17 years underground, then emerge by the billions; prime-number cycles may help them dodge predators.
Animal facts counted in days.A Galápagos tortoise's life: Some live well over a century, and the islands are named after the old Spanish word galápago, meaning tortoise.

Long, longer, longest creatures.Average human (height): The average adult stands under two meters, which makes our height tiny against the giants lower down this list.
Long, longer, longest creatures.Komodo dragon: The largest living lizard has a venomous bite, and females can reproduce without a male in rare cases.
Long, longer, longest creatures.Giraffe (height): A giraffe's neck has the same seven neck bones as ours, but each is extremely long.
Long, longer, longest creatures.Saltwater crocodile: The largest living reptile; males can exceed 6 meters, and they sometimes travel across open ocean.
Long, longer, longest creatures.Reticulated python: This snake is among the longest in the world, though it isn't the heaviest; the green anaconda is far bulkier.
Long, longer, longest creatures.Giant squid: This deep-sea giant has eyes about the size of dinner plates, among the largest in the animal kingdom.
Long, longer, longest creatures.Whale shark: The biggest fish alive, it filters plankton, and its spot pattern is unique to each animal like a fingerprint.
Long, longer, longest creatures.Blue whale: The largest animal known to have ever lived, its heart is about the size of a small car in some estimates.
Long, longer, longest creatures.Lion's mane jellyfish: Its trailing tentacles can be longer than a blue whale, and its sting is painful but rarely dangerous to people.
Long, longer, longest creatures.Bootlace worm: Reports describe this ribbon worm stretching to extraordinary lengths, but it is soft and delicate and the figure is hard to verify.

Natural disasters of the 21st century.Indian Ocean tsunami: On 26 December, a huge quake off Sumatra triggered waves that killed over 200,000 people across a dozen countries.
Natural disasters of the 21st century.Hurricane Katrina: Levee failures flooded about 80 percent of New Orleans.
Natural disasters of the 21st century.Sichuan earthquake: A magnitude 7.9 quake in China left roughly 87,000 dead or missing.
Natural disasters of the 21st century.Haiti earthquake: A shallow 7.0 quake near Port-au-Prince devastated the capital.
Natural disasters of the 21st century.Japan's Tōhoku tsunami: The magnitude 9 earthquake shifted Earth's axis slightly and shortened the day by microseconds.
Natural disasters of the 21st century.Typhoon Haiyan: One of the strongest tropical cyclones ever to make landfall, it struck the Philippines.
Natural disasters of the 21st century.Nepal earthquake: The quake triggered an avalanche at Everest Base Camp that killed 19.
Natural disasters of the 21st century.Hurricane Maria: The storm hit Puerto Rico as a Category 4, and the island's power was out for months.
Natural disasters of the 21st century.Australia's Black Summer: The fires burned over 18 million hectares of Australia.
Natural disasters of the 21st century.Turkey–Syria earthquake: A magnitude 7.8 quake struck on 6 February, killing over 50,000 people in Turkey and Syria.

Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.Bull's-eye (Oliver Twist): The criminal's dog in Dickens' novel belongs to Bill Sikes, and it is a loyal and brutal companion.
Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.Toto: Dorothy's dog in the book was a small terrier, and in the film it was played by a female dog named Terry.
Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.The Hound of the Baskervilles: The hound in Arthur Conan Doyle's story was a huge phantom dog on Dartmoor, and it was made by painting a dog with phosphorus.
Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.Buck (Call of the Wild): The dog in Jack London's story is stolen and sold into the Klondike gold rush, and it eventually answers the call of the wild.
Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.Lassie: The collie was the creation of Eric Knight, and it was played in films by a male dog named Pal.
Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.Snoopy: The beagle in the Peanuts comic strip has an imagination as a World War I flying ace, and a famous doghouse.
Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.Old Yeller: The dog in Fred Gipson's book is a yellow stray, and the story is a children's classic of loyalty.
Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.Clifford the Big Red Dog: The huge red dog in Norman Bridwell's books is as tall as a house, and the character was inspired by his own dog.
Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.Cujo: Stephen King's rabid St Bernard terrorises a mother and son in a car, and it is one of his best-known horror stories.
Famous literary dogs, by first appearanc.Marley: The Labrador in the memoir by John Grogan was known as the world's worst dog, and the book was made into a film.

Nokia phones through the years.Nokia 1011: The Nokia 1011 was the first mass-produced GSM phone, the digital standard that went on to dominate the world.
Nokia phones through the years.Nokia 2110: This model featured the Nokia tune, taken from a guitar piece by Francisco Tárrega, that became the world's most heard ringtone.
Nokia phones through the years.Nokia 9000 Communicator: It was one of the first smartphones, folding open like a clamshell to reveal a keyboard, years before the iPhone.
Nokia phones through the years.Nokia 5110: Interchangeable Xpress-on covers turned phones into fashion items, and the 5110 was a hit for it.
Nokia phones through the years.Nokia 3210: The 3210 was among the first mass-market phones with an internal antenna, and it sold well over 100 million.
Nokia phones through the years.Nokia 3310: The Nokia 3310's legendary toughness became an internet meme, and the phone sold well over 100 million units worldwide.
Nokia phones through the years.Nokia 1100: The 1100 sold about 250 million units, making it one of the best-selling consumer electronic devices ever.
Nokia phones through the years.Nokia N95: The N95 packed a 5-megapixel camera, GPS and Wi-Fi, and was a hit in 2007, the year the iPhone arrived.
Nokia phones through the years.Nokia Lumia 800: This colorful polycarbonate phone ran Windows Phone, the result of Nokia's partnership with Microsoft.
Nokia phones through the years.Nokia Lumia 1020: Its 41-megapixel camera sensor was extraordinary for a phone, letting users zoom in without much loss of quality.

How many letters in each language's alph.Hawaiian: Hawaiian has 13 letters, five vowels and eight consonants, with the okina, a glottal stop, counted as a letter.
How many letters in each language's alph.Italian: Italian traditionally uses 21 letters; J, K, W, X and Y appear only in foreign words such as jeans, whisky and taxi.
How many letters in each language's alph.Hebrew: Hebrew has 22 letters, all consonants, and five of them take a special form at the end of a word.
How many letters in each language's alph.Greek: The Greeks adapted the Phoenician alphabet and added letters for vowels, which the original lacked.
How many letters in each language's alph.English: The ampersand was once recited as the 27th letter of the English alphabet, spoken as and per se and, which became the word ampersand.
How many letters in each language's alph.Spanish: In 2010 the Royal Spanish Academy dropped ch and ll as separate letters, leaving 27, including ñ.
How many letters in each language's alph.Arabic: Arabic has 28 letters, written right to left, and most letters change shape depending on their position in a word.
How many letters in each language's alph.Danish: Danish ends with æ, ø and å, and å replaced the older double a spelling in a 1948 reform, which is why aa still shows up in names.
How many letters in each language's alph.Polish: Polish adds nine letters with diacritics, such as ą, ę and ł, to the Latin alphabet, giving it 32 letters in all.
How many letters in each language's alph.Russian: Cyrillic Russian has 33 letters, including a soft sign and a hard sign that have no sound of their own.

When these companies went public.Ford: Its 1956 IPO, then the biggest ever, ended the family's sole control, though the Fords kept special voting shares.
When these companies went public.McDonald's: Shares were first sold at $22.50 in 1965, and stock splits and dividends have multiplied an early buyer's stake enormously.
When these companies went public.Apple: The December 1980 IPO was the biggest since Ford's and reportedly minted more instant millionaires than any before it.
When these companies went public.Microsoft: Priced at $21 in March 1986, the offering made Bill Gates a billionaire by 1987, aged 31.
When these companies went public.Amazon: It listed in May 1997 at $18 a share, when it was still mainly an online bookshop.
When these companies went public.Google: It used an unusual Dutch auction to sell shares in 2004, letting ordinary investors take part at $85.
When these companies went public.Tesla: It was the first American car company to float since Ford in 1956, priced at $17 a share in June 2010.
When these companies went public.Facebook: Its 2012 Nasdaq debut raised about $16 billion, among the largest tech IPOs, and was marred by trading glitches.
When these companies went public.Alibaba: Its New York listing raised about $25 billion in 2014, then the largest IPO on record.
When these companies went public.Saudi Aramco: Raising around $26 billion, it set a new IPO record and briefly made it the world's most valuable listed company.

Art through the ages, oldest to newest.Venus of Willendorf: A palm-sized limestone figure found in Austria in 1908, it is a famous Stone Age carving, whose purpose remains a mystery.
Art through the ages, oldest to newest.Lascaux cave paintings: Teenagers found the cave in France in 1940. It was closed to the public as visitors' breath damaged the paintings, and a replica built.
Art through the ages, oldest to newest.Tutankhamun's death mask: Made from roughly 10 kilograms of gold, it was found by Howard Carter's team in 1925.
Art through the ages, oldest to newest.Parthenon sculptures: These carvings, also known as the Elgin Marbles, sit in the British Museum, while Greece wants them returned.
Art through the ages, oldest to newest.Terracotta Army: Thousands of life-size soldiers guard the first emperor's tomb, found by farmers digging a well in 1974.
Art through the ages, oldest to newest.Bayeux Tapestry: It is actually an embroidery about 70 metres long telling the story of the Norman Conquest of 1066.
Art through the ages, oldest to newest.Mona Lisa: It became far more famous after being stolen from the Louvre in 1911. It was recovered two years later.
Art through the ages, oldest to newest.The Great Wave off Kanagawa: Hokusai's woodblock print shows a giant wave with Mount Fuji small behind it, and it inspired European Impressionists.
Art through the ages, oldest to newest.Guernica: Picasso painted it in response to the bombing of a Basque town in the Spanish Civil War.
Art through the ages, oldest to newest.Banksy's Girl with Balloon: It shredded itself in the frame just after selling at auction in 2018, and was renamed Love is in the Bin.

When these musicals opened.Show Boat: Kern and Hammerstein's musical tackled racism with a serious, integrated story and moved the form beyond mere revues.
When these musicals opened.Oklahoma!: Rodgers and Hammerstein's first collaboration folded songs and dance into the plot, setting the template for modern musicals.
When these musicals opened.West Side Story: Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim, with choreographer Jerome Robbins, reworked Romeo and Juliet among rival New York gangs.
When these musicals opened.Fiddler on the Roof: Based on Sholem Aleichem's Tevye stories, it was the first Broadway musical to pass 3,000 performances.
When these musicals opened.Chicago: Based on a reporter's 1920s coverage of murderesses, it was directed by Bob Fosse, and its 1996 revival is Broadway's longest-running American show.
When these musicals opened.Cats: Andrew Lloyd Webber set T.S. Eliot's poems about cats to music, and its song 'Memory' became a standard.
When these musicals opened.The Phantom of the Opera: Webber's musical of a disfigured genius haunting the Paris Opera ran on Broadway for 35 years, closing in 2023.
When these musicals opened.Rent: Jonathan Larson's update of La Bohème about struggling New York artists; he died the night before its first preview.
When these musicals opened.Wicked: It retells the Oz story from the witch's point of view, and is based on Gregory Maguire's novel.
When these musicals opened.Hamilton: Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop musical about Alexander Hamilton won the Pulitzer Prize and 11 Tonys.

Classical composers, by birth year.Claudio Monteverdi: His 1607 opera L'Orfeo is among the earliest still regularly performed, bridging Renaissance and Baroque.
Classical composers, by birth year.Antonio Vivaldi: A priest nicknamed the 'Red Priest' for his hair, famed for The Four Seasons.
Classical composers, by birth year.George Frideric Handel: Born in Germany, he made his career in London, and audiences traditionally stand for the Hallelujah chorus of his Messiah.
Classical composers, by birth year.Joseph Haydn: Called the 'Father of the Symphony', he wrote over 100 of them and taught Beethoven.
Classical composers, by birth year.Franz Schubert: He died at 31 yet wrote over 600 songs, and his 'Unfinished' symphony has two movements.
Classical composers, by birth year.Richard Wagner: His four-opera Ring cycle runs about 15 hours, and the Bayreuth theatre was built for it.
Classical composers, by birth year.Johannes Brahms: A perfectionist, he took about 20 years to finish his first symphony, in Beethoven's shadow.
Classical composers, by birth year.Claude Debussy: His piano piece 'Clair de Lune' is typical of the Impressionist style that bent harmony away from tradition.
Classical composers, by birth year.Igor Stravinsky: The Rite of Spring's 1913 Paris premiere reportedly provoked a near-riot.
Classical composers, by birth year.Dmitri Shostakovich: He wrote under Soviet pressure, with 15 symphonies and 15 string quartets, hiding sly irony.

Brand names that became words: debut yea.Aspirin: Bayer lost the trademark in the US and UK after World War I, so aspirin became a generic word.
Brand names that became words: debut yea.Ping-Pong: The name imitates the sound of the ball, and it was trademarked by a British firm, which is why Parker Brothers later sold "Ping-Pong" sets.
Brand names that became words: debut yea.Thermos: Scottish chemist James Dewar invented the vacuum flask but never patented it, and the brand name lost its protection in the US in 1963.
Brand names that became words: debut yea.Band-Aid: Earle Dickson made the first ones at home for his clumsy wife, and he was a Johnson & Johnson employee, who later became a vice president.
Brand names that became words: debut yea.Kleenex: It was first sold as a cold-cream remover and wasn't marketed for noses until later, when people kept using it that way.
Brand names that became words: debut yea.Tupperware: Earl Tupper's airtight plastic bowls sold poorly in stores until home-party sales, led by Brownie Wise, made them a hit.
Brand names that became words: debut yea.Zamboni: Frank Zamboni built the first ice-resurfacing machine for his California rink, and it's now an icon of hockey games.
Brand names that became words: debut yea.Frisbee: The flying disc took its name from the Frisbie Pie Company, whose tins students tossed, and Wham-O launched it as a toy.
Brand names that became words: debut yea.Jet Ski: Kawasaki's trademark for the personal watercraft is used as a generic term, though the maker prefers "personal watercraft".
Brand names that became words: debut yea.Post-it Note: 3M scientist Spencer Silver made a weak glue that seemed useless until a colleague, Art Fry, used it to keep a bookmark in his hymnal.

Horror classics that started franchises.Psycho: Hitchcock reportedly bought up copies of the source novel to protect the twist, and the shower scene took about a week to film.
Horror classics that started franchises.Night of the Living Dead: George Romero's low-budget zombie film never used the word 'zombie', and its sequels made it the template for the modern undead genre.
Horror classics that started franchises.The Exorcist: William Friedkin's film was reportedly so unsettling that some audiences fainted, and it was the first horror movie nominated for Best Picture.
Horror classics that started franchises.The Texas Chain Saw Massacre: Despite its title, the film shows very little blood, and it was inspired in part by the real crimes of Wisconsin killer Ed Gein.
Horror classics that started franchises.Halloween: John Carpenter composed the film's piano theme himself and shot it for a tiny budget, starting the slasher boom and Michael Myers' legacy.
Horror classics that started franchises.Friday the 13th: The first film's killer was Mrs. Voorhees, not Jason, and Jason only became the hockey-masked star by the third film.
Horror classics that started franchises.A Nightmare on Elm Street: Wes Craven reportedly got the idea from news reports about young men dying in their sleep, and the film made Freddy Krueger a horror icon.
Horror classics that started franchises.Child's Play: This film about a killer doll named Chucky turned a toy-company gag into a franchise that is still running.
Horror classics that started franchises.Scream: Wes Craven's meta-slasher poked fun at horror clichés, revived the genre and starts with a famous Drew Barrymore phone-call scene.
Horror classics that started franchises.Saw: James Wan and Leigh Whannell shot the original on a tiny budget, and its Jigsaw character helped spawn a long-running series.

Order these US constitutional amendments.Freedom of speech: Freedom of speech sits in the First Amendment alongside religion, press, assembly and petition, five freedoms in a single sentence.
Order these US constitutional amendments.Right to bear arms: The Second Amendment begins with a clause about a well-regulated militia, and the courts have debated its meaning for centuries.
Order these US constitutional amendments.Right to remain silent: The Fifth Amendment is why police say 'you have the right to remain silent', and it also guarantees due process and bans double jeopardy.
Order these US constitutional amendments.Abolition of slavery: Ratified in 1865 after the Civil War, it formally ended slavery, except as punishment for a crime.
Order these US constitutional amendments.Equal protection: The Fourteenth Amendment guarantees equal protection and citizenship, and it was used in the Brown v. Board of Education decision.
Order these US constitutional amendments.Federal income tax: The Sixteenth Amendment let Congress tax incomes, after the Supreme Court struck down an earlier income tax as unconstitutional.
Order these US constitutional amendments.Prohibition: The Eighteenth banned making and selling alcohol, but it didn't forbid drinking, and it fueled speakeasies and organized crime.
Order these US constitutional amendments.Women's suffrage: Ratified in 1920 after decades of activism by suffragists, it said the right to vote can't be denied on account of sex.
Order these US constitutional amendments.Repeal of Prohibition: The Twenty-First is the only amendment that repealed another, and it was approved by state conventions rather than legislatures.
Order these US constitutional amendments.Voting age lowered: Ratified in 1971 during the Vietnam War, it lowered the voting age to 18, after the slogan 'old enough to fight, old enough to vote'.

When these royal houses took their thron.Habsburgs take Spain: Charles inherited Spain, and later as Charles V ruled an empire on which the sun, so the saying went, never set.
When these royal houses took their thron.Bourbons take France: Henry IV is reputed to have said 'Paris is well worth a Mass', converting to Catholicism to win the throne.
When these royal houses took their thron.Stuarts take England: James VI of Scotland became James I of England on Elizabeth I's death, uniting the two crowns.
When these royal houses took their thron.Romanovs take Russia: Sixteen-year-old Michael Romanov was chosen after years of chaos, and his family ruled Russia until 1917.
When these royal houses took their thron.Braganzas take Portugal: Portugal broke from Spanish rule after 60 years, and John IV became its king.
When these royal houses took their thron.Qing take China: The Manchu rulers took Beijing as the Ming collapsed, and made men wear the queue braid as a sign of loyalty.
When these royal houses took their thron.Hanoverians take Britain: George I came from Hanover and spoke little English, and the dynasty ruled until Victoria's death in 1901.
When these royal houses took their thron.Bernadottes take Sweden: A former French marshal under Napoleon, Charles XIV John founded the dynasty that still reigns in Sweden.
When these royal houses took their thron.House of Windsor named: George V swapped the German name Saxe-Coburg and Gotha for Windsor amid anti-German feeling in World War I.
When these royal houses took their thron.Pahlavis take Iran: Reza Shah, a former army officer, founded the dynasty in 1925; it ended with the revolution of 1979.

Sports history, ancient to modern.First recorded Olympiad: Records say a cook named Coroebus won the only event, a sprint of about 190 m, at the first Games.
Sports history, ancient to modern.Rome's Colosseum opens: It opened under Titus with 100 days of games and seated about 50,000.
Sports history, ancient to modern.Ancient Olympics banned: The ban is traditionally attributed to Emperor Theodosius I, who suppressed pagan festivals.
Sports history, ancient to modern.Scotland bans golf: King James II banned it, because it was distracting men from practising archery.
Sports history, ancient to modern.Earliest written golf rules: The Gentlemen Golfers of Leith in Edinburgh wrote down thirteen rules for a competition.
Sports history, ancient to modern.Queensberry boxing rules: The rules, named for a Marquess, brought in gloves and three-minute rounds, and replaced bare-knuckle brawling.
Sports history, ancient to modern.First Test cricket match: Australia beat England at Melbourne by 45 runs in that first match.
Sports history, ancient to modern.First modern Olympics: Pierre de Coubertin revived the Games in Athens, and the marathon was added to honour a Greek legend.
Sports history, ancient to modern.First televised Olympics: In Berlin, cameras relayed events to viewing halls around the city, though very few could watch.
Sports history, ancient to modern.Olympics held without crowds: The Tokyo Games were delayed a year by the pandemic, and spectators were barred from nearly all venues.

How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.Summit of Mount Everest: Nobody climbed it without bottled oxygen until Messner and Habeler did so in 1978.
How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.Jet airliner cruising: At that height, jet streams can blow winds of hundreds of kilometres an hour, giving planes a boost.
How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.Ozone layer at its densest: The layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet light, and a hole in it was found over Antarctica in 1985.
How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.Baumgartner's 2012 skydive: A balloon carried him up in a pressurised suit, and he fell about 36 km before opening his parachute.
How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.Stratopause: The top of the stratosphere is, perhaps surprisingly, about as warm as freezing.
How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.Noctilucent clouds: These ghostly clouds shine after sunset, being made of ice on meteor dust, and are the highest clouds in the atmosphere.
How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.Kármán line (edge of space): The US Air Force awards astronaut wings from about 80 km, while the international standard is 100 km.
How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.International Space Station: People have lived aboard continuously since November 2000.
How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.Hubble Space Telescope: Edwin Hubble showed that galaxies lie beyond the Milky Way, and the telescope was named after him.
How far up is it? From mountaintop to or.Geostationary orbit: A satellite there orbits once a day, so it hangs over one spot, and so is used for weather and TV.

When these whisky makers were founded.Bushmills: It claims to be the world's oldest licensed distillery, with a royal licence from King James I.
When these whisky makers were founded.Jameson: The Dublin whiskey was founded by a Scotsman, John Jameson, and became one of Ireland's most exported spirits.
When these whisky makers were founded.Laphroaig: Its Islay malt gets a medicinal, smoky taste from peat, and it holds a royal warrant from Prince Charles.
When these whisky makers were founded.Johnnie Walker: Its square bottle and slanted label are iconic, and the brand began in a grocery shop in Kilmarnock.
When these whisky makers were founded.The Glenlivet: It was the first Speyside distillery licensed under the 1823 Excise Act, which legalised distilling.
When these whisky makers were founded.Jack Daniel's: The Tennessee whiskey is filtered through charcoal, and its home county, Moore, is dry.
When these whisky makers were founded.Yamazaki: It was Japan's first malt whisky distillery, near Kyoto, and its whisky has won international prizes.
When these whisky makers were founded.Crown Royal: It was blended for King George VI's 1939 visit to Canada, and comes in a purple bag.
When these whisky makers were founded.Maker's Mark: Each bottle is hand-dipped in red wax, and the bourbon uses soft red winter wheat rather than rye.
When these whisky makers were founded.Kavalan: The Taiwanese distillery matures whisky quickly in warm weather, and won world's best single malt in 2015.

Small mammals on the scale.Etruscan shrew: One of the smallest mammals on Earth; its heart races at well over 800 beats a minute and it eats about its own weight in food daily.
Small mammals on the scale.Harvest mouse: Europe's smallest rodent weaves a ball-shaped nest in tall grass and uses its gripping tail like a fifth limb to climb stems.
Small mammals on the scale.Eastern chipmunk: Cheek pouches let it haul many seeds at once to its burrow, where it hoards food and dozes through cold spells instead of fully hibernating.
Small mammals on the scale.Brown rat: Originally from Asia, it spread worldwide aboard ships; it is the ancestor of white lab rats and can tread water for days.
Small mammals on the scale.European hedgehog: It has roughly 5,000 spines and rolls into a ball when threatened; its insect-heavy diet makes it a gardener's friend.
Small mammals on the scale.European rabbit: Its teeth never stop growing, so constant chewing on fibrous plants wears them down; baby rabbits are born hairless with eyes shut.
Small mammals on the scale.Nine-banded armadillo: Nine-banded armadillos almost always give birth to identical quadruplets, and can hold their breath for minutes to cross streams.
Small mammals on the scale.North American porcupine: It has around 30,000 quills; they can't be shot, but they detach on contact and its tree-climbing skills are surprisingly good.
Small mammals on the scale.Beaver: Its orange teeth are reinforced with iron, and its dams create ponds that reshape whole landscapes and shelter other species.
Small mammals on the scale.Capybara: The world's largest rodent is semi-aquatic and so mellow that birds, monkeys and even caimans are often seen sharing space with it.

How many eggs in one go?.Emperor penguin: Emperor penguins lay a single egg, and the male balances it on his feet through the Antarctic winter while the female feeds at sea.
How many eggs in one go?.Golden eagle: Golden eagles usually lay two eggs, though often only the stronger chick survives, because the older chick may push out the younger one.
How many eggs in one go?.American robin: American robins lay famous blue eggs, which gave the robin's egg blue color its name, and that's about four per clutch.
How many eggs in one go?.Mallard: Mallards lay about ten eggs at once, and the ducklings can leave the nest within a day of hatching.
How many eggs in one go?.Komodo dragon: A female Komodo dragon can reproduce without a male, in a process called parthenogenesis, and she lays about twenty eggs.
How many eggs in one go?.American alligator: American alligators lay about 40 eggs in a mound of vegetation, and the temperature of the nest decides the sex of the babies.
How many eggs in one go?.Green sea turtle: Green sea turtles come ashore to bury eggs in the sand, and only about one in a thousand hatchlings reaches adulthood.
How many eggs in one go?.American bullfrog: A female American bullfrog can lay up to about 20,000 eggs in a floating film at the surface of the water.
How many eggs in one go?.Atlantic cod: A large female Atlantic cod can lay millions of eggs in a single season, though most are eaten before they hatch.
How many eggs in one go?.Ocean sunfish: The ocean sunfish, or Mola mola, is the heaviest bony fish and produces up to about 300 million eggs, the most of any vertebrate.

When these famous protests happened.Peterloo Massacre: Cavalry charged a crowd of about 60,000 gathered in Manchester to demand parliamentary reform; the name mocks the Battle of Waterloo.
When these famous protests happened.Haymarket affair: A rally for the eight-hour day ended in a bomb blast. It is why much of the world marks workers' day on May 1.
When these famous protests happened.Emily Davison at the Derby: The suffragette stepped in front of the King's horse Anmer and died days later, becoming a martyr of the movement.
When these famous protests happened.Jarrow March: About 200 unemployed shipyard workers marched some 450 km from the north of England to London, an effort called the Jarrow Crusade.
When these famous protests happened.Sharpeville massacre: Police opened fire on a protest against South Africa's pass laws, killing 69. The day is now Human Rights Day.
When these famous protests happened.Paris student uprising: Student protests escalated into a general strike of millions. One famous slogan: 'Beneath the paving stones, the beach.'
When these famous protests happened.Stonewall riots: A police raid on a Greenwich Village bar sparked days of unrest. The first Pride marches followed a year later.
When these famous protests happened.Soweto uprising: Students protested Afrikaans being forced on schools. A photo of dying schoolboy Hector Pieterson became an icon of the struggle.
When these famous protests happened.Tiananmen Square protests: Student-led protests in Beijing ended in a military crackdown. The 'Tank Man' photo became a global image of defiance.
When these famous protests happened.Battle of Seattle (WTO): Tens of thousands blocked delegates, forcing the opening ceremony to be cancelled, and launched the anti-globalization movement.

How much power these draw.Electric toothbrush: A toothbrush runs on a tiny battery, and sonic ones vibrate thousands of times a minute. A rechargeable one barely registers on a power meter.
How much power these draw.LED light bulb: LEDs use around 85% less energy than old bulbs for the same light. A 9 W one matches the glow of a 60 W incandescent.
How much power these draw.Phone charger: Fast chargers have grown steadily from 5 W to well over 20 W. Higher power charges a phone to half in about half an hour.
How much power these draw.Old incandescent bulb: Old incandescent bulbs turn only about 5% of power into light, with the rest lost as heat. Many countries have phased them out.
How much power these draw.Gaming PC under load: A powerful gaming PC under load can use as much as a small heater. The graphics card is usually the biggest consumer.
How much power these draw.Microwave oven: A microwave shakes water molecules with waves at 2.45 GHz. That heats the food from the inside out, at least a bit.
How much power these draw.Hair dryer: Hair dryers are among the most power-hungry household items. Most of the energy goes into the heating element.
How much power these draw.UK electric kettle: British kettles are rated around 3 kW. Grid operators watch for "TV pickup" as millions switch kettles on after big shows.
How much power these draw.Home EV charger: A home wall charger at 7.4 kW delivers about 30 miles of range per hour. It runs from a 32-amp single-phase supply.
How much power these draw.Tesla Supercharger: Tesla's Superchargers can deliver up to 250 kW, adding hundreds of kilometres of range in 15 minutes. That's about 100 hair dryers working at once.

When these PC games came out.The Oregon Trail: Created by student teachers in Minneapolis to teach schoolkids about pioneers, it gave the world the line 'You have died of dysentery.'
When these PC games came out.King's Quest: Roberta Williams's adventure for Sierra helped pioneer animated graphics in adventure games, starring the knight Sir Graham.
When these PC games came out.SimCity: Will Wright had trouble finding a publisher because the game had no way to win; it led to The Sims.
When these PC games came out.Civilization: Sid Meier's strategy game popularized 'just one more turn' and let you lead a people from the Stone Age into space.
When these PC games came out.Myst: Its eerie island puzzles helped drive CD-ROM drives into homes, and it was the best-selling PC game of the 1990s.
When these PC games came out.Warcraft: Orcs and Humans: Blizzard's first Warcraft pitted humans against orcs; its world, Azeroth, later became the setting for World of Warcraft.
When these PC games came out.Age of Empires: Ensemble Studios' game takes players from Stone Age villages to the Iron Age, and its series is still popular decades later.
When these PC games came out.Half-Life: Valve's first game starred physicist Gordon Freeman, who never speaks; the studio was founded by former Microsoft employees.
When these PC games came out.RollerCoaster Tycoon: Chris Sawyer wrote nearly all of it himself, in assembly language, which let it run smoothly on very modest PCs.
When these PC games came out.League of Legends: Riot Games' free-to-play hit fills arenas for its Worlds final, held at Beijing's Bird's Nest stadium in 2017.

Kids' TV show premieres.Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Fred Rogers wrote his own songs and always changed into sneakers and a cardigan at the start, an easy routine that ran until 2001.
Kids' TV show premieres.Sesame Street: Created by Joan Ganz Cooney and built on research, it was designed to prepare poorer children for school, with Big Bird as a star.
Kids' TV show premieres.The Muppet Show: It was filmed in England at the studios of a British financier, because no American network would back Jim Henson's idea.
Kids' TV show premieres.Thomas & Friends: Based on the Rev. W. Awdry's Railway Series, the early episodes were narrated by Ringo Starr.
Kids' TV show premieres.Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: It began as a black-and-white comic in 1984; the creators meant it as a parody of other comics.
Kids' TV show premieres.Barney & Friends: The purple dinosaur came from Texas, where Sheryl Leach made home videos for her toddler son.
Kids' TV show premieres.Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: Its action footage was borrowed from a Japanese show, Zyuranger, and mixed with new scenes of American actors.
Kids' TV show premieres.Teletubbies: It was filmed in a real Warwickshire field with sculpted hills, and its Sun Baby was an actual baby's face.
Kids' TV show premieres.Dora the Explorer: Dora introduced many young viewers to Spanish words, helped along by her talking Backpack and Map.
Kids' TV show premieres.Peppa Pig: The British piglet's show is sold in well over 100 countries, and the family live in a house on a hill.

Things that happened on 1 January.Haiti independence: After a slave revolt, Haiti became the first free Black republic, and the first country to permanently abolish slavery.
Things that happened on 1 January.Emancipation Proclamation: Lincoln's order freed enslaved people in Confederate states; it exempted border states, and the 13th Amendment ended slavery entirely.
Things that happened on 1 January.Sudan independence: It was Africa's largest country by area until 2011, when South Sudan split off.
Things that happened on 1 January.Cuban Revolution wins: Fidel Castro's forces took power as the dictator Batista fled Havana; Castro would rule for nearly 50 years.
Things that happened on 1 January.Cameroon independence: French Cameroun became independent; the country is nicknamed Africa in miniature for its range of landscapes and cultures.
Things that happened on 1 January.UK joins the EEC: The UK joined with Ireland and Denmark; the EEC was a forerunner of the EU, which Britain left in 2020.
Things that happened on 1 January.Czechoslovakia splits: The Velvet Divorce created the Czech Republic and Slovakia peacefully, without a referendum.
Things that happened on 1 January.NAFTA takes effect: The US, Canada and Mexico formed a free-trade zone, and on the same day Zapatista rebels rose up in Chiapas.
Things that happened on 1 January.Euro notes and coins: Twelve countries swapped their old currencies for the euro, and people across Europe queued at cash machines for the new notes.
Things that happened on 1 January.Croatia adopts the euro: It became the 20th member of the euro zone and joined the Schengen travel area on the same day.

Gothic and horror books, by year.Frankenstein: Mary Shelley began it at 18 during a ghost-story contest on a rainy holiday near Lake Geneva with Lord Byron.
Gothic and horror books, by year.The Vampyre: John Polidori wrote this story at that same Geneva gathering, creating the aristocratic vampire later made famous by Dracula.
Gothic and horror books, by year.The Legend of Sleepy Hollow: Washington Irving's tale of Ichabod Crane and a headless horseman first appeared in a collection of essays and stories.
Gothic and horror books, by year.Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde: Robert Louis Stevenson reportedly wrote the first draft in just a few days after a vivid nightmare, and the title is now shorthand for a split personality.
Gothic and horror books, by year.The Picture of Dorian Gray: Wilde's only novel was used against him during his trial, and its first version was first published in a magazine.
Gothic and horror books, by year.Dracula: Bram Stoker told the story through diaries and letters, and probably drew the name from Vlad the Impaler, called Dracula.
Gothic and horror books, by year.The Phantom of the Opera: Gaston Leroux, a French journalist, wrote this novel, which inspired many films and the long-running Andrew Lloyd Webber musical.
Gothic and horror books, by year.The Call of Cthulhu: H. P. Lovecraft's story created a cosmic horror monster that still has a huge cult following in games and fiction.
Gothic and horror books, by year.The Shining: Stephen King's novel was inspired by a stay at the Stanley Hotel in Colorado, and he reportedly disliked Kubrick's film version.
Gothic and horror books, by year.It: Stephen King's novel features a shape-shifting entity that most often appears as Pennywise the Clown, and it runs more than a thousand pages.
